## What this package is

`PhysioCore` is a **compatibility package**. The shared data model it used to
implement -- the `PhysioExperiment` S4 class and the containers for multiple
streams, repeated sessions and cohorts -- now lives in the
[PhysioExperiment](https://github.com/x-biosignal/PhysioExperiment) package.
`PhysioCore` re-exports that public interface unchanged, so that existing code
written against it keeps working, including `S4` objects that were saved while
the classes were defined here.

Everything shown below therefore works identically whether you attach
`PhysioCore` (as here) or `PhysioExperiment`. **New code should depend on
`PhysioExperiment` directly;** this vignette exists so that users of the older
package name can see the core workflow in one place.

```{r attach}
library(PhysioCore)
```

## Build a PhysioExperiment

A `PhysioExperiment` holds one or more assays shaped as time x channels, plus a
sampling rate. We create a small synthetic three-channel recording -- no files,
no downloads.

```{r construct}
set.seed(1)
sig <- matrix(rnorm(500 * 3), nrow = 500, ncol = 3)   # 500 samples, 3 channels
pe <- PhysioExperiment(assays = list(raw = sig), samplingRate = 250)
pe
```

## Core accessors

The fundamental properties are reached through accessor functions rather than
slots:

```{r accessors}
samplingRate(pe)   # Hz
nChannels(pe)      # number of channels
duration(pe)       # seconds
head(timeIndex(pe)) # time vector for the samples
channelNames(pe)    # auto-generated names, until you set your own
```

Channels are named `Ch1`, `Ch2`, ... by default. Rename them with the
replacement form of `channelNames()`:

```{r rename}
channelNames(pe) <- c("Fz", "Cz", "Pz")
channelNames(pe)
```

## Channel management

Select or drop channels by name; the returned object is a `PhysioExperiment`:

```{r channels}
front <- pickChannels(pe, c("Fz", "Cz"))
channelNames(front)

no_pz <- dropChannels(pe, "Pz")
channelNames(no_pz)
```

## Events

Experimental markers (stimuli, responses, ...) are attached with `addEvents()`
and read back with `getEvents()`:

```{r events}
pe <- addEvents(pe, onset = c(0.5, 1.2, 1.9), duration = 0.1, type = "stimulus")
nEvents(pe)
getEvents(pe)
```

## Extract a time window

`extractWindow()` cuts a segment by time in seconds:

```{r window}
seg <- extractWindow(pe, tmin = 0, tmax = 0.5)
dim(seg)
```

## Summarize and check for gaps

```{r summary}
summary(pe)
naSummary(pe)
```

## Where to go next

`PhysioCore` adds nothing beyond this re-exported surface. For the full data
model -- including the multi-stream, longitudinal and cohort containers -- and
for signal I/O, preprocessing and analysis, see the dedicated packages:

| Package | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `PhysioExperiment` | the data model (depend on this in new code) |
| `PhysioIO` | reading/writing files and databases |
| `PhysioPreprocess` | filtering, referencing, resampling, ICA |
| `PhysioAnalysis` | spectral/time-frequency analysis, statistics, plots |

```{r session, echo = FALSE}
sessionInfo()
```
